ruling.recommended_action: Refund $3.68 (excess distance fare) to the rider's original payment method; issue the driver a notification-duty reminder for the uninformed reroute and log it on his route-compliance record (no formal warning, first incident)
ruling.reasoning:
Safety screen: the complaint, chat and driver statement contain no threat, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation; dispute type is route_deviation. safety_concern = none.

Route arithmetic (RD-1): actual 10.1 km − recommended 7.692 km = 2.408 km deviation, well over the 1 km tolerance, so a refund is due under RD-2.

Segments (RD-3/RD-4/RD-5): (1) The early Sentosa leg (PALAWAN BEACH WALK → BEACH VIEW → ARTILLERY AVENUE, ~14:17:20–14:18:50). The optimal route runs PALAWAN BEACH WALK → SILOSO BEACH WALK → BEACH VIEW → ARTILLERY AVENUE; the driver used Palawan Beach Walk instead of the parallel Siloso Beach Walk, a short corridor substitution of well under 0.5 km — map-matching noise under RD-1's 0.2 km-segment rule, and in any event covered by the rider's later request to "go via Canning Lane" and immaterial. No traffic reason exists for it (no traffic events; speed bands there are 4–5, i.e. free-flow). It is counted within the single excess figure below. (2) The middle leg (SENTOSA GATEWAY → KAMPONG BAHRU ROAD → HOSPITAL DRIVE → EU TONG SEN STREET) essentially follows the recommended corridor: the optimal route also uses SENTOSA GATEWAY/TELOK BLANGAH ROAD and the whole of KAMPONG BAHRU ROAD. (3) At 14:29:10, already on EU TONG SEN STREET, the rider asked "Can you go via Canning Lane and drop me at the other side of Clarke Quay instead?" There is no driver reply and no in-app destination edit, so no accepted destination change and no $3.00 fee — and the driver did not in fact drive Canning Lane (the telemetry shows CANTONMENT ROAD → LIM TECK KIM ROAD → ANSON ROAD → CECIL STREET). Under RD-5 a rider request sent after the segment began does not count as prior consent; Canning Lane was not driven, so the words do not cover the segment anyway. The driver's claim that "the GPS rerouted" me is not borne out: traffic_speed_bands show EU TONG SEN STREET at band 4 and KAMPONG BAHRU ROAD at band 5 during the trip — free-flowing, not bands 1–2 — and there are no traffic events, so RD-4 gives no traffic reason. The reroute is therefore without justification and the excess is refundable.

Amount (RD-2): excess distance fare = refundable km × this trip's per-km distance fare. Per-km rate = distance_fare 14.24 ÷ 10.1 km = $1.4099/km. The whole deviation lies in the congested-fare city portion, so 2.408 km × $1.4099 = $3.395, rounded $3.40. Note the deviation also added time-fare (4.4 s of the 16 min is the traffic portion); time fare, tolls (0.0) and surge (1.0, no differential) are not refunded. Precedent alignment: DISP-2026-0089 (uninformed reroute) — partial refund of the excess distance fare; DISP-001 ($3.44 on 4.3 km at $0.80/km) — same outcome shape, different per-km rate. Confidence lowered from 0.9 to 0.82 because the record contains no explicit optimal route for the final approach to Clarke Quay, so the exact excess-km split of the ~2.4 km deviation is estimated rather than measured; the outcome (refund_partial) is not affected. Below $10 → system-final (TH-1/TH-2, C1). The driver has no upheld route deviation in 90 days, so RD-6 does not add a flag_account.

segment_findings.reason: Post-16:10 reroute from EU TONG SEN STREET toward Clarke Quay via CANTONMENT ROAD → LIM TECK KIM ROAD → ANSON ROAD → CECIL STREET (14:26:50–14:29:55). The rider's only route message came at 14:29:10, after the segment had begun ('Can you go via Canning Lane…'), and no driver reply/acceptance exists. RD-5: notice/consent after the segment starts does not count; RD-3 requires driver acceptance, which is absent. RD-4 traffic reason is also absent — EU TONG SEN STREET shows speed_band 4 during the trip (RD-4 needs bands 1–2), no traffic events, and the driver's 'GPS rerouted me' claim is unsupported. So the excess km here count as deviation.

Early Sentosa leg (14:17:20–14:18:50) showing PALAWAN BEACH WALK → BEACH VIEW → ARTILLERY AVENUE instead of the optimal PALAWAN BEACH WALK → SILOSO BEACH WALK → BEACH VIEW → ARTILLERY AVENUE; speed bands 4–5, no traffic events, so no RD-4 traffic reason. No prior rider consent was given for this route (the driver's chat at 14:15:50 was an arrival message only), so any excess km here count. The corridor substitution is short (well under 0.5 km) and is captured within the single 2.408 km excess figure rather than being separately quantified.

The only road the rider named (Canning Lane at 14:29:10) was never driven — the telemetry shows CECIL STREET, not Canning Lane, on the final approach — so nothing in the rider's message exempted any segment. Recorded as the rider-named-road check under RD-5 (named_road absent from the roads driven → not covered).

rejected_claims.reason: Traffic data shows free-flowing conditions (bands 4–5) on the roads used and no traffic events on the replaced sections, so the claimed GPS/traffic reroute is unsupported (RD-4). The driver also did not state he had told the rider before deviating (RD-5).
Substantially correct: the recommended/estimated distance is 7.692 km against an actual 10.1 km; the rider's rounding is immaterial and the excess is refunded on the measured figures.
